dicas.texto: Você está no caminho certo! Se cada copo inteiro tem 4 partes de um quarto, quantas partes de um quarto existem em 2 copos inteiros?
Tente multiplicar a parte inteira (2) pelo denominador (4) e depois somar com o numerador da fração (3) para encontrar o total de quartos.
Você tem 8 quartos nos dois copos inteiros. Agora, adicione os 3 quartos que sobraram. Qual o total de quartos?
Você tem 8/4 + 3/4. Somando os numeradores, você chega no valor final que deve colocar na caixa de cima, mantendo o denominador 4 embaixo.

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta "What is the fraction in the problem?" com duas caixas numéricas (f1 em cima = numerador, f2 embaixo = denominador); reta numérica de 0 a 3 (numline) onde o aluno marca um ponto, com encaixe em 4 partes por unidade (marcas ocultas); texto de apoio na reta: "The number hint is off in this problem!"; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (digitar nos campos, converter, marcar o ponto, concluir).

reta numérica; o aluno adiciona um ponto (marca a posição da fração)

campo numérico da caixa de cima da fração (numerador)
campo numérico: parte inteira do número misto

dicas.texto: First separate the full cups from the fractional part of the extra cup.
Represent the whole amount as an integer followed by a fraction with numerator 3 and denominator 4.
The integer part counts the completely filled cups, while the fraction describes the remaining part.
Show two complete units and select three of the four equal parts in the fraction model.
An improper fraction represents the same quantity as the mixed number, but with one numerator over one denominator.
To ..., multiply the whole-number part by the denominator, add the numerator, and keep the denominator.
Use the whole-number part and the denominator of the fractional part before adding the fractional numerator.
Complete the conversion by combining the two whole units, each made of four fourths, with the three additional fourths.
The numerator counts how many equal fractional parts are in the entire amount.
Multiply the whole-number part by the denominator, then add the numerator of the fractional part.
Convert the two whole cups into fourths by multiplying 2 by 4, then include the 3 extra fourths.
Add the eight fourths from the whole cups to the three fourths that remain, and type that total in f1.
The denominator tells how many equal parts make one whole.
Use the number of equal parts named in the fractional portion of the problem.
The leftover amount is described in fourths, so the denominator must match that partition.
Count the equal parts in the extra cup and type that count in the lower field, f2.
Locate the point after two whole units because the amount contains two full cups.
Divide the numerator by the denominator to determine the decimal position on the number line.
The target lies between 2 and 3, at the third quarter mark after 2.
On the four-part interval from 2 to 3, click the third hidden-quarter position after 2.
Before submitting, check that the fraction and the number-line point represent the same quantity.
Review the numerator, denominator, and marked position from left to right.
Confirm that f1 contains the numerator, f2 contains the denominator, and the point is between 2 and 3.
When the fraction fields and the number-line point are complete, press the ... button once.

exercicio.statement:
Every morning, Lili's mother prepares a pitcher of tomato juice for Lili and her sister. One morning, Lili's mother made the pitcher a bit too large; it completely filled Lili's cup, her sister's up, and the left over filled about 3/4 of a third cup. Show the number of cups of tomato juice Lili's mother prepared that morning on the number line.
What is the fraction in the problem?
